question.text: From what date is every new investment made by an AIF required to be held in dematerialised form, irrespective of whether it is made directly in the investee company or acquired from another entity?

answer.text: From April 1, 2023, as per SEBI Circular of June 21, 2023.
From July 1, 2024, as clarified by SEBI.
From January 1, 2025, as per the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 amendment.
From October 21, 2021, via the Merchant Banker PPM circular.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI has clarified that any investment made by an AIF on or after July 1, 2024, shall be held in dematerialised form only, irrespective of whether the investment is made directly in the investee company or is acquired from another entity. The AIF accordingly opens a demat account with an NSDL/CDSL DP. The Trap: The June 21, 2023 circular pertains to dematerialised issuance of units of the AIF to investors — a different trigger. October 21, 2021 is the merchant-banker PPM filing modality circular. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests both the unit-demat rule (Jun 2023) and the investment-demat rule (Jul 2024). Do not conflate the two — unit demat is about UNITS the AIF issues to LPs; investment demat is about SECURITIES the AIF holds in investee companies. Manager's Pro-Tip: Align your custodian-DP onboarding timeline with deal closing, not after. A signed SHA but pending demat account will stall settlement. Keep at least one CDSL and one NSDL DP on panel for flexibility.
